description: We are a team of 5 people, 4 in high school and 1 in middle school, being educated at METU DF Schools. This is our second time at the Nasa Space Apps Challange and our hopes and motivation is high for it!
summary: As Ekulast, we developed a simulation that gives researchers or students all the conditions of a selected landmark/landmarks'. 'The Lunar South Pole Site Navigator' site also gives the user the chance to compare the chosen landmarks' conditions, choose a path between them and see the distance between those points. Our site is important because of it providing all the information needed for landing on the south pole clearly and accessible. These moon investigations conducted by the said scientists in the challange can help with future projects that could be important for humanity.
details: As Ekulast, we have developed a Lunar South Pole Navigator encapsulating the area formed by the 80 degrees South parallels which allows both the public to view previous Apollo Missions and the Moon’s geomorphological landmarks, and the specialized mission squads to access extensive information, including the standard variation formula of calculated temperature in Kelvin based on inputted emissivity values, and mapped using an uploaded DEM file. This also means that an improvement or change in NASA data can be mapped with the same navigator system. It shows azimuth, slope and earth viewing windows, and can be used to guess the conditions of the lunar environment for a future date. Using these values, it also suggests both the best/safest route for transport due to the limitations of equipment, and the fastest yet riskiest path. Positions of the sun and earth are present for all situations and the full globe can be seen on overview for precise Apollo locations. Coordinates may also be entered via professionals to accurately choose points, and practical shortcuts such as CTRL+Z is mobilized for easy maneuvering in the site. Our site is important because of it providing all the information needed for landing on the south pole clearly and accessible. Latitude, longitude, distance to the South Pole, slope, sky view %, % of the times sun is seen in 30 days, the nearest crater and the distance to that crater, the temperature in K, Sun angle, azimuth, elevation, terrain horizon, above horizon, max angle of light in next 30 days, Sun disc ⌀, time of sunrise, time that Earth can be visible, graphs of the visibility window, graph of the temperature and the locations of the Earth and the Sun of the choosen landing mark. Our goal in creating this website is to assist with potential experiments, space landings, and research by providing the necessary information to the scientists who will use it. This assistance we provide could perhaps support discoveries that would be a major advancement for humanity. Furthermore, our platform empowers student users to learn, self-develop, and effortlessly access knowledge by offering comprehensive resources, including detailed explanations of all concepts utilized in the lunar pole simulation within our 'Scientifics' section, alongside verified information regarding the Moon sourced directly from NASA’s official website. Our project features numerous innovative elements that distinguish it from other platforms. As previously mentioned, one key feature is the 'Scientific' section. By defining all terminology utilized throughout the site, this section significantly saves time for students and curious learners, eliminating the need to browse multiple websites to research unfamiliar concepts. Additionally, as stated before, this section presents lunar data sourced directly from NASA’s official website, allowing users to gain a deeper understanding of the reasoning behind the simulation's data and comprehend the simulation itself much more thoroughly. We considered to make a practical and more modern interface compared to the NASA Trek. Furthermore, we tried to make our website usable for educational purposes.
